items.quote: Proteo Crisps launches in France in March 2026 in Paris, Lyon and Lille, targeting weekly sport practitioners: 17.5 million adults, with 41% purchase intent for a similar concept.
The French protein snack category is worth 480 million euros in 2024 and grows about 11% per year (2021-2024) [1].
Plant-based products account for 18% of the category [1], and 27% of French adults bought a protein snack in the last three months [1].
Supermarkets and hypermarkets hold 68% of protein snack sales, specialised sport and organic shops 17%, online 9%, and gyms and vending 6% [1].
The savoury snack market overall is worth 2.9 billion euros [1].

A web source reports that hyperprotein foods sold in French supermarkets reached about 380 million euros in 2024 [2]; this covers a broader scope than snacks and is not directly comparable with the 480 million euro snack figure.

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The target (SEG1, 17.5M adults, 41% intent) is compared with the other segments by size and intent, and goals such as the 2% share are cited. The channel mix follows the 68%/17% channel shares. The one gap is pricing, which is left undecided ("not yet decidable") apart from a premium-to-private-label direction.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: The messages reflect the positioning (crisp-style protein, six ingredients, unlike sport bars) and use only the five strategy channels, with sport and gym messages aimed at SEG1. The supermarket and organic messages are fairly generic and not specific to sport practitioners. The "Ma pause du midi" and ingredient-list content leans toward office workers, which is the stated secondary audience.

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The primary target (office workers plus sport practitioners who snack at work), the supermarket-led channels (68%), the positioning against Barebells and Gerble, and the vegan decision (small base, 1.3M, 2.5%, used as advocates) all follow from the segment and competitor analysis with figures. Minor gaps: sport practitioners are the largest and highest-intent group but are placed secondary even though the plan merges them with office workers, and pricing is only directional because no benchmark exists, though the plan says so openly.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: Messages match the positioning ("crunchy snack that happens to be high in protein"), the everyday-snacker target and the strategy channels (in-store, gyms, organic, online), and the visuals avoid gym-heavy imagery. Minor gaps: social media and PR are not listed as channels in the strategy, and the "aperitif" and founder-story content is somewhat generic.

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The commuter target follows from the segment figures (11.4M × 34% ≈ 3.9M vs. 0.38M for specialty), the 3,500-POS goal and the channel data (24% + 13% + 54%). The plan holds the price as a working price and names the validation gap. One minor gap: the secondary student target is justified only by "same outlets", although the plan itself says there is no channel data for students.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: Messages fit the commuter target and positioning (18-hour cold brew, no added sugar, oat, "für den Weg zum Gleis") and use only the four strategy channels. Minor gaps: the supermarket and online messages are generic product-fact messages rather than commuter-specific ones, and the Vanilla lead is not backed by the analysis. The content ideas also add social video and out-of-home, which are not strategy channels.
